newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end up on firm cash prices, bellies down.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end up on firm cash prices, bellies down.

text.p: CME hog futures ended higher Tuesday, lifted by gains in cash hog markets and renewed bullish speculative interest, while pork belly futures settled lower, CME floor traders said.
Hogs at most Midwestern cash markets sold at firm to higher prices, underpinned by tight supplies of market-ready animals, cash-connected traders said.
However, gains in the hog pit were curbedby profit taking following Monday's near-limit gains and a "wait and see" attitude from traders after the market's big rally, pit traders said.
"We had a big up-move on Monday, so what the market is doing now is just digesting the move and seeing what's ahead," one Chicago-based analyst said.
Traders were expecting cash hogs to trade at steady to slightly higher prices on Wednesday, cash sources said.

Despite expectations for higher cash prices Wednesday, bearish traders cautioned that the rain sweeping through the Corn Belt on Tuesday could spur a jump in the number of market-ready hogs and end up pressuring prices.
"We had a pretty extensive weather system across much of the Midwest, which might give farmers more time to sort and ship hogs," said Alaron Trading Corp analyst, Chuck Levitt.
In later trade, commercials were said to be buyers. The hog market also went through some technical levels that attracted commodity funds buying, a floor source said.
Earlier, Cargill, LIT and FIMAT Futures, Inc. were noted seller in the hog pit, traders said.

Expectations for a jump in the amount of pork bellies moving into warehouses outside Chicago registered with the CME, combined with local selling to push pork bellies to a lower close, traders in that pit said.
Traders had been looking for the CME to show a net in movement up to 2.0 million lbs. But after the close, the CME reported a net-in movment of 1.143 million lbs.

Hogs ended down 0.100 to up 0.200 cent a lb, with December up 0.175 at 54.050 cents. February was up 0.200 at 74.025. February pork bellies were down 0.650 cent at 69.400. Other months closed down 0.500 to 0.800.
